key_idea: Compositions ac with c built from primes just above P_2(a) also give pairwise disjoint L-sets, and because they are self-similar to the L_a this caps how much density elements with P(a)^{1+v}>a can carry at about sqrt(v); integrating this distribution-function bound against the 1/(1+v) savings gives the pi/4 factor.
reason: The conceptual core is attractive: Erdős's disjoint-density argument is sharpened by a self-similarity trick into a sqrt(v) cumulative bound, and summation by parts turns that into the integral pi/4, which explains where the constant comes from. But the full deduction of Theorem 2 rests on explicit numerical tables, monotone bounds for mu_q, special handling of the prime 2, and constant chasing, so a clean idea ends up carried by substantial bookkeeping.
recognized: Lichtman, 'A proof of the Erdős primitive set conjecture' (2022/2023)
